signature:
NLAlib.Assembly.completion_factor_mono {q k s : ℝ} (hq : 0 ≤ q) (hqk : q ≤ k) (hks : k < s - 1) :
  q / (s - q - 1) ≤ k / (s - k - 1)
name: NLAlib.Assembly.completion_factor_mono
doc:
Monotonicity of the completion factor (Chen–Persson, proof of `thm:GN`): `q ↦ q/(s−q−1)`
is increasing for `q < s − 1`, so the factor of `lem:completion` for dimension `q ≤ k` is at
most that for `k`. Helper for atlas `gn-expected-error`.

signature:
NLAlib.Assembly.gn_assembly.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} {X Y cfac : Ω → ℝ}
  {cmax B : ℝ} (hY : 0 ≤ Y) (hcmax : 0 ≤ cmax) (hc : ∀ (ω : Ω), cfac ω ≤ cmax)
  (hcond : ∫ (ω : Ω), X ω ∂μ = ∫ (ω : Ω), cfac ω * Y ω ∂μ) (hYbound : ∫ (ω : Ω), Y ω ∂μ ≤ B)
  (hcYi : MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun ω => cfac ω * Y ω) μ) (hYi : MeasureTheory.Integrable Y μ) :
  ∫ (ω : Ω), X ω ∂μ ≤ cmax * B
name: NLAlib.Assembly.gn_assembly
doc:
Abstract assembly of Chen–Persson, Theorem `thm:GN` (Tropp–Webber 2023, Thm 5.1).
* `X = ‖A − Â‖_F²`, `Y = ‖(I − QQᵀ)A‖_F²` (the range-finder error),
  `cfac ω = 1 + q(ω)/(s − q(ω) − 1)` with `q = rank(AΩ)` the (random) number of columns of `Q`.
* `hcond` encodes `lem:completion` after the tower property (conditioning on `Ω`, using
  independence of `Ψ` and `Ω`): `E X = E[(1 + q/(s−q−1)) Y]`.
* `hc` is the deterministic bound `q ≤ t` and monotonicity of `q ↦ q/(s−q−1)`
  (`completion_factor_mono`).
* `hYbound` is the range-finder theorem (`thm:RSVD`).
Atlas `gn-expected-error`.

signature:
NLAlib.Assembly.gn_explicit.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω}
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {X Y cfac Zsq : Ω → ℝ} {k t s OPTsq : ℝ} (hk : 0 ≤ k) (hkt : k + 2 ≤ t)
  (hts : t + 2 ≤ s) (hY : 0 ≤ Y) (hc : ∀ (ω : Ω), cfac ω ≤ 1 + t / (s - t - 1))
  (hcond : ∫ (ω : Ω), X ω ∂μ = ∫ (ω : Ω), cfac ω * Y ω ∂μ) (hstruct : ∀ (ω : Ω), Y ω ≤ OPTsq + Zsq ω)
  (hZ : ∫ (ω : Ω), Zsq ω ∂μ = k / (t - k - 1) * OPTsq) (hcYi : MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun ω => cfac ω * Y ω) μ)
  (hYi : MeasureTheory.Integrable Y μ) (hZi : MeasureTheory.Integrable Zsq μ) :
  ∫ (ω : Ω), X ω ∂μ ≤ (1 + t / (s - t - 1)) * ((1 + k / (t - k - 1)) * OPTsq)
name: NLAlib.Assembly.gn_explicit
doc:
Chen–Persson, Theorem `thm:GN` (Tropp–Webber 2023, Thm 5.1), expectation level:
`t ≥ k+2`, `s ≥ t+2`,
`E‖A − Â‖_F² ≤ (1 + t/(s−t−1)) (1 + k/(t−k−1)) ‖A − ⟦A⟧ₖ‖_F²`.
Hypotheses: `hc` (`lem:completion`'s factor with `q = rank(AΩ) ≤ t`), `hcond`
(`lem:completion` + tower property), `hstruct` (`prop:hmt-struct` for
`Y = ‖(I−QQᵀ)A‖_F²`), `hZ` (`lem:moments` + `lem:invmom`, as in the proof of `thm:RSVD`).
The hypothesis `hk` is not used by the arithmetic; it is kept for fidelity.
Atlas `gn-expected-error` (uses `rsvd-expected-error`).

name: NLAlib.Assembly.integral_le_sqrt_integral_sq
doc:
Jensen's inequality in the form used throughout Chen–Persson: for a nonnegative
square-integrable random variable `Y`, `E Y ≤ √(E Y²)`. Proved from
`0 ≤ Var Y = E Y² − (E Y)²`. Helper for atlas `rsvd-expected-error` (Frobenius-norm,
unsquared form of HMT 2011, Thm 10.5).

signature:

  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {X Zsq : Ω → ℝ} {OPTsq c : ℝ} (hX : ∀ (ω : Ω), X ω ≤ OPTsq + Zsq ω)
  (hZ : ∫ (ω : Ω), Zsq ω ∂μ = c * OPTsq) (hXi : MeasureTheory.Integrable X μ) (hZi : MeasureTheory.Integrable Zsq μ) :
  ∫ (ω : Ω), X ω ∂μ ≤ (1 + c) * OPTsq
name: NLAlib.Assembly.rsvd_assembly
doc:
Assembly of Chen–Persson, Theorem `thm:RSVD` (HMT 2011, Thm 10.5, Frobenius case).
* `X = ‖A − Â‖_F²`, `Zsq = ‖Σ₂ Ω₂ Ω₁†‖_F²`, `OPTsq = ‖Σ₂‖_F² = ‖A − ⟦A⟧ₖ‖_F²`.

  `E ‖Σ₂ Ω₂ Ω₁†‖_F² = ‖Σ₂‖_F² · k/(t−k−1)`; here with a general constant `c`.
Atlas `rsvd-expected-error`.

signature:
NLAlib.HansonWrightProof.hanson_wright_inequality.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω}
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {n : ℕ} {A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ} {X : Fin n → Ω → ℝ} {K C t : ℝ}
  (hK : 0 < K) (hC : 0 < C) (hC_domain : 4 * Real.exp 1 ≤ C) (hC_diag_quad : 8 * Real.exp 1 ^ 3 ≤ C)
  (hC_offdiag_domain : 16 * Real.exp 1 ≤ C ^ 2) (hC_offdiag_quad : 64 * Real.exp 1 ^ 2 ≤ C)
  (hF : 0 < NLAlib.HansonWrightProof.deterministicFrobeniusNorm A)
  (hOp : 0 < NLAlib.HansonWrightProof.deterministicOperatorNorm A) (h_indep : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun X μ)
  (hX_subG : ∀ (i : Fin n), ProbabilityTheory.HasSubgaussianMGF (X i) ⟨K ^ 2, ⋯⟩ μ) (ht : 0 ≤ t) :
  (μ {ω | t ≤ |NLAlib.HansonWrightProof.centeredQuadraticForm μ A X ω|}).toReal ≤
    2 *
      Real.exp
        (-(1 / (4 * C)) *
          min (t ^ 2 / (K ^ 4 * NLAlib.HansonWrightProof.deterministicFrobeniusNorm A ^ 2))
            (t / (K ^ 2 * NLAlib.HansonWrightProof.deterministicOperatorNorm A)))

doc:
Hanson-Wright tail bound with the MGF certificate proved from sub-Gaussian coordinates.

This theorem does not take `HasHansonWrightMGF` as a hypothesis.  Instead it proves
that certificate from independence and coordinate sub-Gaussian MGF bounds, then
optimizes the resulting Chernoff bound.

        0 ≤ t →
          (μ {ω | t ≤ |NLAlib.HansonWrightProof.centeredQuadraticForm μ A X ω|}).toReal ≤

name: NLAlib.HansonWrightProof.hasHansonWrightMGF_of_bounded
doc:
A proved Hanson-Wright MGF certificate for bounded coordinates.

If each coordinate satisfies `|Xᵢ| ≤ K` almost surely, then the quadratic form lies
in the interval `[-K²‖A‖₁, K²‖A‖₁]`.  The centered quadratic form is therefore
bounded by `2K²‖A‖₁`; the local bounded MGF lemma above gives a quadratic CGF
estimate.  The explicit side condition compares this bounded-coordinate constant
with the Frobenius-scale constant used by the Hanson-Wright tail statement.

signature:
NLAlib.HasEuclideanLogSobolev.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure (ι → ℝ))
  (c : ℝ) : Prop
name: NLAlib.HasEuclideanLogSobolev
doc:
A probability measure satisfies the Euclidean logarithmic Sobolev inequality with
constant `c` if `Ent(g²)≤2c∫|∇g|²` for every `C¹` test function whose displayed integrals
are finite. The gradient is the standard coordinate Dirichlet form.
Ledoux 2001, Theorem 5.1; atlas `herbst` (general LSI premise).

signature:

  {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure (ι → ℝ)} {c : ℝ} {motive : NLAlib.HasEuclideanLogSobolev μ c → Sort u}
  (t : NLAlib.HasEuclideanLogSobolev μ c)
  (mk :
    (constant_nonneg : 0 ≤ c) →
      (inequality :
          ∀ (g : (ι → ℝ) → ℝ),
            ContDiff ℝ 1 g →
              MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => g x ^ 2) μ →
                MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => g x ^ 2 * Real.log (g x ^ 2)) μ →
                  MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => ∑ i, (fderiv ℝ g x) (Pi.single i 1) ^ 2) μ →
                    ∫ (x : ι → ℝ), g x ^ 2 * Real.log (g x ^ 2) ∂μ -
                        (∫ (x : ι → ℝ), g x ^ 2 ∂μ) * Real.log (∫ (x : ι → ℝ), g x ^ 2 ∂μ) ≤
                      2 * c * ∫ (x : ι → ℝ), ∑ i, (fderiv ℝ g x) (Pi.single i 1) ^ 2 ∂μ) →
        motive ⋯) :
  motive t
name: NLAlib.HasEuclideanLogSobolev.casesOn

  {B C : Matrix n m ℝ} (hB : NLAlib.IsMoorePenroseInverse A B) (hC : NLAlib.IsMoorePenroseInverse A C) : B = C
name: NLAlib.IsMoorePenroseInverse.unique
doc:
The Moore–Penrose inverse is unique, also for zero-rank and empty matrices.
Horn–Johnson §7.3; atlas `pseudoinverse`.

signature: NLAlib.IsRademacher.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω) (r : Ω → ℝ) : Prop
name: NLAlib.IsRademacher
doc: `r` has the Rademacher law under `μ`: `μ.map r = ½ δ₁ + ½ δ₋₁`. Tropp 2015, §4.1.

signature:
NLAlib.IsSVD {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) (U : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) ℝ) (V : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) :
  Prop
name: NLAlib.IsSVD
doc:
`IsSVD A U V`: `U`, `V` are orthogonal and `A = U Σ Vᵀ` with `Σ = rectDiag (singularValues A)`
(Horn–Johnson 2013, Thm 2.6.3; HMT 2011, §2.1). The `k`-th columns of `U` and `V` are the
left/right singular vectors for `σ_k`. Atlas `svd`.

name: NLAlib.IsSVD.apply
doc:
Thin-SVD / outer-product expansion, entrywise:
`A i j = ∑_{k < min m n} σ_k U_{ik} V_{jk}`, i.e. `A = ∑_k σ_k u_k v_kᵀ`
(Horn–Johnson 2013, §2.6; HMT 2011, §2.1). Atlas `svd`.

signature:
NLAlib.IsSVD.casesOn.{u} {m n : ℕ} {A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ} {U : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) ℝ}
  {V : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ} {motive : NLAlib.IsSVD A U V → Sort u} (t : NLAlib.IsSVD A U V)
  (mk :
    (transpose_mul_left : U.transpose * U = 1) →
      (transpose_mul_right : V.transpose * V = 1) →
        (eq : A = U * NLAlib.rectDiag (NLAlib.singularValues A) * V.transpose) → motive ⋯) :
  motive t
name: NLAlib.IsSVD.casesOn

signature:
NLAlib.IsSVD.eq {m n : ℕ} {A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ} {U : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) ℝ} {V : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ}
  (self : NLAlib.IsSVD A U V) : A = U * NLAlib.rectDiag (NLAlib.singularValues A) * V.transpose
name: NLAlib.IsSVD.eq
doc: The factorization `A = U Σ Vᵀ`.

signature:
NLAlib.IsSVD.eq_head_add_tail {m n : ℕ} {A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ} {U : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) ℝ}
  {V : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ} (h : NLAlib.IsSVD A U V) (k : ℕ) :
  A =
    (U * NLAlib.rectDiag fun i => if i < k then NLAlib.singularValues A i else 0) * V.transpose +
      (U * NLAlib.rectDiag fun i => if i < k then 0 else NLAlib.singularValues A i) * V.transpose
name: NLAlib.IsSVD.eq_head_add_tail
doc:
Block SVD split at index `k` (HMT 2011, §2.1, `A = U₁Σ₁V₁ᵀ + U₂Σ₂V₂ᵀ`): the head
`U Σ_{<k} Vᵀ` (the truncated SVD) plus the tail `U Σ_{≥k} Vᵀ`. Atlas `svd`.

name: NLAlib.IsSVD.frobSq_sub_truncatedMatrix
doc:
The squared error of the truncated SVD is exactly the singular-value
tail, with no rank/dimension side conditions.
Horn–Johnson Theorem 7.4.9; atlas `eckart-young`.

signature:
NLAlib.IsSVD.isBestRankApprox_truncatedMatrix {m n : ℕ} {A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ} {U : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) ℝ}
  {V : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ} (h : NLAlib.IsSVD A U V) (k : ℕ) : NLAlib.IsBestRankApprox k A (h.truncatedMatrix k)
name: NLAlib.IsSVD.isBestRankApprox_truncatedMatrix
doc:
**Frobenius Eckart–Young minimizer.** Truncating any actual SVD gives a
best rank-at-most-`k` approximation, rather than assuming a best-approximation
predicate. Horn–Johnson Theorem 7.4.9; atlas `eckart-young`.

name: NLAlib.IsSVD.isMoorePenroseInverse
doc:
An SVD produces the Moore–Penrose inverse by reciprocating its nonzero
singular values; scalar `0⁻¹ = 0` handles zero singular values.
Horn–Johnson §7.3; atlas `pseudoinverse`.

name: NLAlib.IsSVD.mk
NLAlib.IsSVD.moorePenroseInverse_eq
doc:
Any real SVD computes the same Moore–Penrose inverse, independently of the
choice of singular vectors. Horn–Johnson §7.3; atlas `pseudoinverse`.

name: NLAlib.IsSVD.mulVec_dotProduct_mulVec_eq_sum
doc:
The SVD gives the squared length as a weighted sum in right-singular
coordinates. Atlas: `svd`, `norm-lipschitz`.

signature:
NLAlib.IsSVD.mul_right {m n : ℕ} {A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ} {U : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) ℝ}
  {V : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ} (h : NLAlib.IsSVD A U V) : A * V = U * NLAlib.rectDiag (NLAlib.singularValues A)
name: NLAlib.IsSVD.mul_right
doc: `A V = U Σ`, i.e. `A vₖ = σₖ uₖ`. Atlas `svd`.

signature:
NLAlib.IsSVD.mul_transpose_left {m n : ℕ} {A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ} {U : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) ℝ}
  {V : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ} (h : NLAlib.IsSVD A U V) : U * U.transpose = 1
name: NLAlib.IsSVD.mul_transpose_left
doc: `U Uᵀ = I`. Atlas `svd`.

signature:
NLAlib.IsSVD.mul_transpose_right {m n : ℕ} {A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ} {U : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) ℝ}
  {V : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ} (h : NLAlib.IsSVD A U V) : V * V.transpose = 1
name: NLAlib.IsSVD.mul_transpose_right
doc: `V Vᵀ = I`. Atlas `svd`.

name: NLAlib.IsSVD.mul_transpose_self
doc:
`AAᵀ = U diag(σ₀², …, σₘ₋₁²) Uᵀ`: the left singular vectors diagonalize `AAᵀ`.
Atlas `svd`.

signature:
NLAlib.IsSVD.rank_truncatedMatrix_le {m n : ℕ} {A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ} {U : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) ℝ}
  {V : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ} (h : NLAlib.IsSVD A U V) (k : ℕ) : (h.truncatedMatrix k).rank ≤ k
name: NLAlib.IsSVD.rank_truncatedMatrix_le
doc:
The truncated SVD has rank at most its cutoff, including cutoff zero.
Horn–Johnson Theorem 7.4.9; atlas `eckart-young`.

signature:
NLAlib.IsSVD.recOn.{u} {m n : ℕ} {A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ} {U : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) ℝ}
  {V : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ} {motive : NLAlib.IsSVD A U V → Sort u} (t : NLAlib.IsSVD A U V)
  (mk :
    (transpose_mul_left : U.transpose * U = 1) →
      (transpose_mul_right : V.transpose * V = 1) →
        (eq : A = U * NLAlib.rectDiag (NLAlib.singularValues A) * V.transpose) → motive ⋯) :
  motive t
name: NLAlib.IsSVD.recOn
NLAlib.IsSVD.transpose_eq
doc:
`Aᵀ = V Σᵀ Uᵀ`: an SVD of the transpose (the singular values agree by
`singularValues_transpose`). Atlas `svd`.

name: NLAlib.IsSVD.transpose_mul
doc: `Uᵀ A = Σ Vᵀ`, i.e. `Aᵀ uₖ = σₖ vₖ`. Atlas `svd`.

signature:
NLAlib.IsSVD.transpose_mul_left {m n : ℕ} {A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ} {U : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) ℝ}
  {V : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ} (self : NLAlib.IsSVD A U V) : U.transpose * U = 1
name: NLAlib.IsSVD.transpose_mul_left
doc: `U` is orthogonal.

name: NLAlib.IsSVD.transpose_mul_mul
doc: `Uᵀ A V = Σ`. Atlas `svd`.

signature:
NLAlib.IsSVD.transpose_mul_right {m n : ℕ} {A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ} {U : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) ℝ}
  {V : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ} (self : NLAlib.IsSVD A U V) : V.transpose * V = 1
name: NLAlib.IsSVD.transpose_mul_right
doc: `V` is orthogonal.

name: NLAlib.IsSVD.transpose_mul_self
doc:
`AᵀA = V diag(σ₀², …, σₙ₋₁²) Vᵀ`: the right singular vectors diagonalize the Gram matrix
(Horn–Johnson 2013, §2.6). Atlas `svd`.

signature:
NLAlib.IsSVD.truncatedMatrix {m n : ℕ} {A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ} {U : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) ℝ}
  {V : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ} (_h : NLAlib.IsSVD A U V) (k : ℕ) : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ
name: NLAlib.IsSVD.truncatedMatrix
doc:
Truncate a given real SVD after its first `k` singular values. The index
may exceed either matrix dimension; in that case padding handles the cutoff.
Horn–Johnson Theorem 7.4.9; atlas `eckart-young`.

signature: NLAlib.IsStandardGaussian.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω) (g : Ω → ℝ) : Prop
name: NLAlib.IsStandardGaussian
doc: `g` has the standard Gaussian law under `μ`: `μ.map g = gaussianReal 0 1`. Tropp 2015, §4.1.

signature:
NLAlib.IsSubspaceEmbedding.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {k : Type u_1} {m : Type u_2} {d : Type u_3} [Fintype k] [Fintype m]
  [Fintype d] (S : Matrix k m ℝ) (U : Matrix m d ℝ) (ε : ℝ) : Prop
name: NLAlib.IsSubspaceEmbedding
doc:
`S` is an `ε`-subspace embedding for `range U`: `(1 - ε)‖Ux‖² ≤ ‖SUx‖² ≤ (1 + ε)‖Ux‖²` for
every `x`. Woodruff 2014 §2.1; Martinsson–Tropp 2020 §8.7. Atlas: `ose-def`.

signature:
NLAlib.IsSubspaceEmbedding.mono.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {k : Type u_1} {m : Type u_2} {d : Type u_3} [Fintype k] [Fintype m]
  [Fintype d] {S : Matrix k m ℝ} {U : Matrix m d ℝ} {ε ε' : ℝ} (h : NLAlib.IsSubspaceEmbedding S U ε) (hεε' : ε ≤ ε') :
  NLAlib.IsSubspaceEmbedding S U ε'
name: NLAlib.IsSubspaceEmbedding.mono
doc:
Monotonicity in the distortion: an `ε`-embedding is an `ε'`-embedding for `ε ≤ ε'`.

Atlas: `ose-def`.

name: NLAlib.IsSubspaceEmbedding.mul_right
doc:
Basis independence, easy direction: an embedding for `range U` is an embedding for
`range (U C)` for any `C` (since `range (U C) ⊆ range U`).

Atlas: `ose-def`.

name: NLAlib.IsSubspaceEmbedding.of_mul_right
doc:
Basis independence, converse direction: if `C` has a right inverse `D` (`C D = 1`, so
`range (U C) = range U`) then an embedding for `range (U C)` is an embedding for `range U`.

Atlas: `ose-def`.

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ)
  (xs : n → ℝ) : (n → ℝ) → ℕ → ℝ
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr
doc:
Expected squared error `E‖x_k - xs‖²` after `k` randomized Kaczmarz steps started at `x`,
rows drawn i.i.d. with probabilities `prob A`. Defined by first-step recursion:
`expErr 0 x = ‖x - xs‖²`, `expErr (k+1) x = ∑ i, prob A i * expErr k (step A b x i)`.
See `expErr_eq_sum_paths` for the path-sum form. Atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr_eq_sum_paths.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ)
  (b : m → ℝ) (xs x : n → ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr A b xs x k =
    ∑ ω,
      (∏ j, NLAlib.Kaczmarz.prob A (ω j)) * (NLAlib.Kaczmarz.run A b k ω x - xs) ⬝ᵥ (NLAlib.Kaczmarz.run A b k ω x - xs)
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr_eq_sum_paths
doc:
`expErr` is the expectation over i.i.d. row sequences: the sum over all `ω : Fin k → m` of
`(∏ j, prob A (ω j)) * ‖run A b k ω x - xs‖²`. Atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr_le.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ)
  (b : m → ℝ) (xs : n → ℝ) (hxs : A.mulVec xs = b) (σ : ℝ)
  (hσ : ∀ (v : n → ℝ), σ ^ 2 * v ⬝ᵥ v ≤ A.mulVec v ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec v) (x : n → ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr A b xs x k ≤ (1 - σ ^ 2 / NLAlib.frobSq A) ^ k * (x - xs) ⬝ᵥ (x - xs)
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr_le
doc:
**Randomized Kaczmarz converges linearly in expectation.**
Strohmer–Vershynin 2009, Thm 2; atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.
If `A *ᵥ xs = b` and `σ² ‖v‖² ≤ ‖A v‖²` for all `v`, then after `k` steps with rows drawn
i.i.d. with probability `‖A i‖² / ‖A‖_F²`,
`E‖x_k - xs‖² ≤ (1 - σ² / ‖A‖_F²)^k ‖x₀ - xs‖²`.
Deviations from the printed statement: SV09 take `A` of full column rank and `σ = ‖A⁻¹‖⁻¹`
(rate `1 - κ(A)⁻²`); here `σ` is any constant satisfying `hσ` (the sharp choice is
`σ_min(A)`, atlas `courant-fischer`), and no rank or nonzero-row assumption is needed.

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr_succ.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ)
  (b : m → ℝ) (xs x : n → ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr A b xs x (k + 1) =
    ∑ i, NLAlib.Kaczmarz.prob A i * NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr A b xs (NLAlib.Kaczmarz.step A b x i) k
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr_succ
doc: Unfolding `expErr` at `k + 1` steps (first-step analysis). Atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr_zero.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ)
  (b : m → ℝ) (xs x : n → ℝ) : NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr A b xs x 0 = (x - xs) ⬝ᵥ (x - xs)
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr_zero
doc: Unfolding `expErr` at `0` steps. Atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expected_sqErr_step_eq.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ) (xs x : n → ℝ) (hxs : A.mulVec xs = b) (hA : A ≠ 0) :
  ∑ i, NLAlib.Kaczmarz.prob A i * (NLAlib.Kaczmarz.step A b x i - xs) ⬝ᵥ (NLAlib.Kaczmarz.step A b x i - xs) =
    (x - xs) ⬝ᵥ (x - xs) - A.mulVec (x - xs) ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec (x - xs) / NLAlib.frobSq A
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expected_sqErr_step_eq
doc:
One-step expected error identity:
`∑ i, prob A i * ‖step A b x i - xs‖² = ‖x - xs‖² - ‖A (x - xs)‖² / ‖A‖_F²` for `A ≠ 0`.
Strohmer–Vershynin 2009, proof of Thm 2; atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expected_sqErr_step_le.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ) (xs x : n → ℝ) (hxs : A.mulVec xs = b) (σ : ℝ)
  (hσ : ∀ (v : n → ℝ), σ ^ 2 * v ⬝ᵥ v ≤ A.mulVec v ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec v) :
  ∑ i, NLAlib.Kaczmarz.prob A i * (NLAlib.Kaczmarz.step A b x i - xs) ⬝ᵥ (NLAlib.Kaczmarz.step A b x i - xs) ≤
    (1 - σ ^ 2 / NLAlib.frobSq A) * (x - xs) ⬝ᵥ (x - xs)
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expected_sqErr_step_le
doc:
One-step contraction of randomized Kaczmarz: if `σ² ‖v‖² ≤ ‖A v‖²` for all `v`
(`σ` a lower bound on the smallest singular value, atlas `courant-fischer`), then
`∑ i, prob A i * ‖step A b x i - xs‖² ≤ (1 - σ² / ‖A‖_F²) ‖x - xs‖²`.
No hypothesis on `A` (for `A = 0` the left side is `0` and the rate is `1`).
Strohmer–Vershynin 2009, proof of Thm 2; atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.

signature: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.prob.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (i : m) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.prob
doc:
Row-selection probability `‖A i‖² / ‖A‖_F²` of randomized Kaczmarz.
Strohmer–Vershynin 2009, Algorithm; atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.prob_nonneg.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ)
  (i : m) : 0 ≤ NLAlib.Kaczmarz.prob A i
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.prob_nonneg
doc: Selection probabilities are nonnegative. Atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.rate_nonneg.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [Nonempty n]
  (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (σ : ℝ) (hσ : ∀ (v : n → ℝ), σ ^ 2 * v ⬝ᵥ v ≤ A.mulVec v ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec v) :
  0 ≤ 1 - σ ^ 2 / NLAlib.frobSq A
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.rate_nonneg
doc:
The contraction factor is nonnegative when `n` is nonempty: `σ² ≤ ‖A‖_F²`.
Atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.run.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  (Fin k → m) → (n → ℝ) → n → ℝ
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.run
doc:
The iterate after applying the steps with rows `ω 0, ω 1, …, ω (k-1)` in that order,
starting from `x`. Atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.run.eq_def.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ) (x✝ : ℕ)
  (x✝¹ : Fin x✝ → m) (x✝² : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.Kaczmarz.run A b x✝ x✝¹ x✝² =
    match (motive := (x : ℕ) → (Fin x → m) → (n → ℝ) → n → ℝ) x✝, x✝¹, x✝² with
    | 0, x, x_1 => x_1
    | k.succ, ω, x => NLAlib.Kaczmarz.run A b k (Fin.tail ω) (NLAlib.Kaczmarz.step A b x (ω 0))
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.run.eq_def

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.sqErr_step.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ)
  (xs x : n → ℝ) (hxs : A.mulVec xs = b) (i : m) :
  (NLAlib.Kaczmarz.step A b x i - xs) ⬝ᵥ (NLAlib.Kaczmarz.step A b x i - xs) =
    (x - xs) ⬝ᵥ (x - xs) - (A i ⬝ᵥ (x - xs)) ^ 2 / A i ⬝ᵥ A i
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.sqErr_step
doc:
Pythagoras for one Kaczmarz step (the step is an orthogonal projection onto a hyperplane
containing `xs`): `‖step A b x i - xs‖² = ‖x - xs‖² - (A i ⬝ᵥ (x - xs))² / ‖A i‖²`.
Holds for every row; for a zero row both sides equal `‖x - xs‖²`.
Strohmer–Vershynin 2009, proof of Thm 2; atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.step.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ) (x : n → ℝ)
  (i : m) : n → ℝ
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.step
doc:
One Kaczmarz step on row `i`: the orthogonal projection of `x` onto the hyperplane
`{y | A i ⬝ᵥ y = b i}`. For a zero row the step is the identity (real division by zero is `0`).
Strohmer–Vershynin 2009, Algorithm (eq. (2)); atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.step_sub_solution.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ)
  (xs x : n → ℝ) (hxs : A.mulVec xs = b) (i : m) :
  NLAlib.Kaczmarz.step A b x i - xs = x - xs - (A i ⬝ᵥ (x - xs) / A i ⬝ᵥ A i) • A i
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.step_sub_solution
doc:
Error recursion of one Kaczmarz step when `A *ᵥ xs = b`:
`step A b x i - xs = (x - xs) - ((A i ⬝ᵥ (x - xs)) / ‖A i‖²) • A i`.
Strohmer–Vershynin 2009, proof of Thm 2; atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.sum_paths_le.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ)
  (b : m → ℝ) (xs : n → ℝ) (hxs : A.mulVec xs = b) (σ : ℝ)
  (hσ : ∀ (v : n → ℝ), σ ^ 2 * v ⬝ᵥ v ≤ A.mulVec v ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec v) (x : n → ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  ∑ ω,
      (∏ j, NLAlib.Kaczmarz.prob A (ω j)) *
        (NLAlib.Kaczmarz.run A b k ω x - xs) ⬝ᵥ (NLAlib.Kaczmarz.run A b k ω x - xs) ≤
    (1 - σ ^ 2 / NLAlib.frobSq A) ^ k * (x - xs) ⬝ᵥ (x - xs)

doc:
Path-sum form of SV09 Thm 2: the weighted average over all row sequences of length `k` of
the squared error is at most `(1 - σ² / ‖A‖_F²)^k ‖x - xs‖²`.
Strohmer–Vershynin 2009, Thm 2; atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.

name: NLAlib.OperatorConvexOn
doc:
`f` is operator convex on the convex set `I`: `f (t A + (1-t) H) ≼ t f(A) + (1-t) f(H)` for all
Hermitian `A`, `H` of every size with spectra in `I`. Tropp 2015, Def. 8.4.6. Atlas:
`operator-monotone-convex`.

signature:

doc:
Operator Jensen inequality for an isometry: if `f` is operator convex on `I` and `Kᴴ K = 1`, then

Tropp 2015, Thm 8.5.2 (single-isometry form). Atlas: `operator-monotone-convex`. Ported from the
Prove2me mission *An Introduction to Matrix Concentration Inequalities, Ch 8*.

name: NLAlib.completion_reduction
doc:
**Exact Gaussian completion, deterministic reduction** (Chen–Persson, Lemma
`lem:completion`; Tropp–Webber 2023, proof of Thm 5.1).

Fixed `Q` (orthonormal columns, `q ≥ 1`), its orthogonal completion `Qp = Q⊥`
(`QQᵀ + Q⊥Q⊥ᵀ = I`), fixed `A`, random `Ψ` with `s ≥ q + 2`; `G₁ ω = Ψ ωᵀ Q`,
`G₂ ω = Ψ ωᵀ Q⊥`, `E = residual Q A = (I − QQᵀ)A`.
* `hG₁`: `G₁` has full column rank a.s. (so `G₁†G₁ = I`), the "almost surely" of the paper;
* `hG₂`: `E‖G₁†G₂(Q⊥ᵀE)‖_F² = E‖G₁†‖_F² · ‖Q⊥ᵀE‖_F²` — `lem:moments` for `G₂` conditionally
  on `G₁` (independence of `G₁`, `G₂`) followed by the tower property;
* `hG₁m`: `E‖G₁†‖_F² = q/(s−q−1)` — `lem:invmom` (needs `s ≥ q+2`, `q ≥ 1`);
* `hGi`: integrability of the noise term.
Everything else in the paper's proof (`ΨᵀA = G₁QᵀA + G₂Q⊥ᵀE`, `X̂ = QᵀA + G₁†G₂Q⊥ᵀE`,
Pythagoras, `‖Q⊥ᵀE‖_F = ‖E‖_F`) is proved in `SketchedRegression.lean` and used here.
Conclusion: `eq:completion`,
`E‖A − Q(ΨᵀQ)†ΨᵀA‖_F² = (1 + q/(s−q−1)) ‖(I − QQᵀ)A‖_F²`.
Atlas `gn-expected-error` (helper; uses `sketched-regression`, `orthonormal-completion`).

      (∀ (j : Fin (k - n)), (H.mulVec fun l => V l j) = 0) ∧
        ∀ (g : Fin k → ℝ),
          g ⬝ᵥ g - H.mulVec g ⬝ᵥ (H * H.transpose)⁻¹.mulVec (H.mulVec g) = ∑ j, V.transpose.mulVec g j ^ 2

doc:

orthonormal basis `V` (`k × (k - n)`, `Vᵀ V = 1`) of `ker H` writes the squared distance from `g`
to the row space of `H` as `‖g‖² - (H g)ᵀ (H Hᵀ)⁻¹ (H g) = ‖Vᵀ g‖²`; the columns of `V` are
killed by `H`.

Helper for Tropp–Webber 2023, Lemma B.2 / HMT 2011, Prop A.5 (law of the residual of a Gaussian
row and its independence from the regression). Atlas: `inverse-wishart-mean` (helper). Ported
from the Prove2me solutions `Sol_GaussianMatrix_residual_law` and
`GaussianMatrix.regression_residual_indep` (the two copies merged, keeping the stronger
statement).

if `range Q₁ ⊆ range Q₂`, written `Q₁ = Q₂ C`, then `‖(I − Q₂Q₂ᵀ)A‖_F² ≤ ‖(I − Q₁Q₁ᵀ)A‖_F²`.
Deviation: only `Q₂` needs orthonormal columns; `Q₁` is arbitrary (with `residual` defined
by the formula `A − Q₁Q₁ᵀA`). Atlas `projection-facts`.

name: NLAlib.frobSq_residual_le_of_range_subset
doc:
**Deterministic range-finder bound, Frobenius form** (HMT 2011, Thm 9.1, squared Frobenius
case): if `A = U₁Σ₁V₁ᵀ + U₂Σ₂V₂ᵀ`, `Ω₁ = V₁ᵀΩ` has full row rank, `Ω₂ = V₂ᵀΩ`, `QᵀQ = I` and
`range(AΩ) ⊆ range(Q)`, then `‖(I − QQᵀ)A‖_F² ≤ ‖Σ₂‖_F² + ‖Σ₂Ω₂Ω₁†‖_F²`.
Chen–Persson, Prop. `prop:hmt-struct`, second inequality (LRA `hmt_second_frob`).

Deviations from the printed statement: the SVD is a block decomposition with only the
hypotheses the proof uses (`U₂ᵀU₂ = I`, `V₁ᵀV₁ = I`, `V₂ᵀV₂ = I`, `V₁ᵀV₂ = 0`; no diagonality,
no conditions on `U₁`); `P_Y` is `QQᵀ` for any orthonormal `Q` with `range(AΩ) ⊆ range(Q)`
(HMT take `range Q = range(AΩ)`); index types are arbitrary `Fintype`s. Atlas
`hmt-9-1-frobenius`.

signature:

`‖A − QB‖_F² = ‖(I − QQᵀ)A‖_F² + ‖QᵀA − B‖_F²` (proof of HMT 2011, Thm 9.1; LRA
`pythagoras_range`). Atlas `projection-facts`.

signature:
NLAlib.frobSq_sub_mul_le_of_isBestRankApprox.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {q : Type u_3} [Fintype m]

doc:
`Q ⟦QᵀA⟧ₖ` is a best rank-`k` Frobenius approximation of `A` among matrices `QB` with
`rank B ≤ k` (HMT 2011, proof of Thm 9.1; LRA `best_in_range`). Atlas `projection-facts`.

name: NLAlib.frobSq_sub_mul_le_of_isBestRankApprox_of_range_subset
doc:
**Truncated range-finder bound** (Chen–Persson, Prop. `prop:hmt-struct`, third inequality;
LRA `hmt_third`): under the hypotheses of `frobSq_residual_le_of_range_subset`, for any best
rank-`k` approximation `Y` of `QᵀA`, `‖A − QY‖_F² ≤ ‖Σ₂‖_F² + ‖Σ₂Ω₂Ω₁†‖_F²`. Here `k` is the
number of columns of `V₁`. Deviation: index types other than `Fin k` are arbitrary `Fintype`s.
Atlas `hmt-9-1-frobenius` (truncated variant).

name: NLAlib.frobSq_sub_mul_pinvR_mul_transpose_eq
doc:
The rank-`≤ k` competitor `Z = AΩΩ₁†V₁ᵀ` satisfies `A − Z = U₂Σ₂V₂ᵀ − U₂Σ₂Ω₂Ω₁†V₁ᵀ`
and hence `‖A − Z‖_F² = ‖Σ₂‖_F² + ‖Σ₂Ω₂Ω₁†‖_F²` (HMT 2011, proof of Thm 9.1; Chen–Persson,
proof of `prop:hmt-struct`). Atlas `hmt-9-1-frobenius`.

signature:

doc:
Untruncated-vs-truncated comparison (Chen–Persson, remark after `thm:RSVD` / proof of
`rsvd_main`): the RSVD output error is bounded by the tRSVD output error, pointwise, for any
`Y` (in particular `Y = ⟦QᵀA⟧ₖ`). A restatement of
`NLAlib.frobSq_residual_le_frobSq_sub_mul` (LRA `frobSq_residual_le`) with the residual
written out. Atlas `rsvd-expected-error`.

signature:

actual rank-`k` optimum plus squared projection error. The small truncated SVD
is the proved minimizer, so no best-approximation certificate is assumed.
HMT 2011, §9.2; atlas `truncation-lemma` (ordinary projected component).
Frobenius contraction gives coefficient `1` on the projection error.

literal truncated-SVD output. HMT 2011, §9.2; atlas `truncation-lemma`
(ordinary projected component). This follows from the stronger coefficient-one
bound and includes all target ranks and empty shapes.

signature:
NLAlib.gammaRatio_le {r k : ℕ} (hr : 1 ≤ r) (hrk : r ≤ k) :
  2 ^ ((↑k - ↑r - 1) / 2) * Real.Gamma ((↑k + 1) / 2) / (Real.Gamma (↑r / 2) * Real.Gamma (↑k - ↑r + 1)) ≤
    ((↑k + ↑r) / 2) ^ ((↑k - ↑r + 1) / 2) / (2 * Real.Gamma (↑k - ↑r + 1))
name: NLAlib.gammaRatio_le
doc:
**Gamma-ratio estimate.** For `1 ≤ r ≤ k`,
`2^{(k-r-1)/2} Γ((k+1)/2) / (Γ(r/2) Γ(k-r+1)) ≤ ((k+r)/2)^{(k-r+1)/2} / (2 Γ(k-r+1))`,
i.e. the constant of the density bound (B.5) is at most the constant of (B.6).

Tropp–Webber 2023, (B.6). Atlas: `wishart-lambda-min-tail` (helper). Proof: iterated Gautschi
inequality (log-convexity of `Γ`, Bohr–Mollerup) and AM–GM (`prod_range_add_le_pow`). Ported
from Prove2me solution `GaussianMatrix.tw_gamma_ratio_bound`.

signature:
NLAlib.gamma_inverse_spectral_endpoint_le {r k : ℕ} (hr : 1 ≤ r) (hrk : r < k) :
  2 ^ (-(↑k - ↑r) / 2) * Real.pi * Real.Gamma (↑k / 2) / (Real.Gamma (↑r / 2) * Real.Gamma ((↑k - ↑r + 1) / 2) ^ 2) ≤
    (Real.exp 1 ^ 2 * (↑k + ↑r - 1) / (2 * (↑k - ↑r) ^ 2)) ^ ((↑k - ↑r) / 2)
name: NLAlib.gamma_inverse_spectral_endpoint_le
doc:
The endpoint quadratic-probe constant for an `r × k` Gaussian matrix
is bounded by the strengthened inverse spectral moment constant.
Source: direct quadratic-probe proof, endpoint moment calculation; the
arithmetic-progression mean retains `k+r-1`. Atlas:
`inverse-wishart-spectral-moment` (helper).

signature:

name: NLAlib.gamma_probe_mellin_residue_eq
doc:
Duplication turns the operator Mellin residue into the hard-edge density constant.
Source: Legendre duplication, operator rederivations Section 5; atlas
`wishart-lambda-min-tail` (exact constant helper).

signature:
NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_indepFun_block {n k r t : ℕ} (V₁ : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin k) ℝ) (V₂ : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin r) ℝ)
  (hV₁ : V₁.transpose * V₁ = 1) (hV₂ : V₂.transpose * V₂ = 1) (hV₁₂ : V₁.transpose * V₂ = 0) :
  ProbabilityTheory.IndepFun (fun G => Matrix.of.symm (V₁.transpose * Matrix.of G))
    (fun G => Matrix.of.symm (V₂.transpose * Matrix.of G)) (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix n t)
name: NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_indepFun_block
doc:
**Independence of Gaussian blocks.** If `V₁` (`n × k`) and `V₂` (`n × r`) have orthonormal
columns and `V₁ᵀ V₂ = 0`, and `G` is an `n × t` standard Gaussian matrix, then `V₁ᵀ G` and
`V₂ᵀ G` are independent.

HMT 2011 (Halko–Martinsson–Tropp), §10.2 (`Ω₁ = V₁ᵀ Ω` and `Ω₂ = V₂ᵀ Ω` are independent).
Atlas: `block-law-indep`. Ported from the Prove2me workspace, Gaussian Random Matrices
series.

signature:
NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_lt_frobSq_pinvR_le {r k : ℕ} (hrk : r + 4 ≤ k) (t : ℝ) (ht : 1 ≤ t) :
  (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix r k) {G | 12 * ↑r / (↑k - ↑r) * t < NLAlib.frobSq (NLAlib.pinvR (Matrix.of G))} ≤
    ENNReal.ofReal (4 * t ^ (-((↑k - ↑r) / 2)))
name: NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_lt_frobSq_pinvR_le
doc:
**Tail bound for the Frobenius norm of the Gaussian pseudoinverse.** For an `r × k`
standard Gaussian matrix `G` with `r + 4 ≤ k` and `t ≥ 1`,
`P[‖G†‖_F² > 12 r t/(k-r)] ≤ 4 t^{-(k-r)/2}`, with `G† = pinvR G`.

HMT 2011, Thm A.6 (used in Prop 10.4; HMT state it as `P[‖Ω₁†‖_F ≥ √(12k/p) t] ≤ 4 t^{-p}`
with `Ω₁` of size `k × (k+p)`, the same bound after `t ↦ √t`). Atlas: `pinv-frob-tail`.
Proof: each diagonal entry of `(G Gᵀ)⁻¹` is `1/χ²_{k-r+1}`
(`gaussianMatrix_map_inv_self_mul_transpose_apply_self`), whose `L^{(k-r)/2}` norm is at most
`3/(k-r+1)` (`integrable_and_integral_rpow_inv_sum_sq_gaussianReal_lt`, atlas
`chi-square-neg-moment`); Minkowski's inequality bounds `‖tr (G Gᵀ)⁻¹‖_{L^q}` and Markov's
inequality gives the tail. Ported from Prove2me solution `GaussianMatrix.pinv_frobenius_tail`.

signature:
NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_lt_specNorm_pinvR_le {r k : ℕ} (hr : 2 ≤ r) (hrk : r ≤ k) (t : ℝ) (ht : 0 < t) :
  (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix r k) {G | t < NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.pinvR (Matrix.of G))} ≤
    ENNReal.ofReal
      (1 / √(2 * Real.pi * (↑k - ↑r + 1)) * (Real.exp 1 * √↑k / (↑k - ↑r + 1)) ^ (↑k - ↑r + 1) * t ^ (-(↑k - ↑r + 1)))
name: NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_lt_specNorm_pinvR_le
doc:
**Tail bound for the spectral norm of the Gaussian pseudoinverse.** For an `r × k`
standard Gaussian matrix `G` with `2 ≤ r ≤ k` and `t > 0`,
`P[‖G†‖ > t] ≤ (2π(k-r+1))^{-1/2} (e√k/(k-r+1))^{k-r+1} t^{-(k-r+1)}`,
with `G† = pinvR G`.

HMT 2011, Prop A.3; Chen–Dongarra 2005, Lemma 4.1. Atlas: `pinv-spectral-tail`. Proof:
`‖G†‖² = ‖(G Gᵀ)⁻¹‖ = 1/σ_min(Gᵀ)²` (`specNorm_pinvR_sq`,
`specNorm_inv_self_mul_transpose_eq`, atlas `pseudoinverse`), the `λ_min` lower tail
(`gaussianMatrix_sigmaMin_transpose_sq_le_le`, atlas `wishart-lambda-min-tail`, which uses the
proved operator bound (B.5)) and Stirling's formula. Ported from Prove2me solution
`GaussianMatrix.pinv_spectral_tail`.

signature:
NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_map_block {n k t : ℕ} (V₁ : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin k) ℝ) (hV₁ : V₁.transpose * V₁ = 1) :

    NLAlib.gaussianMatrix k t
name: NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_map_block
doc:
**Law of a Gaussian block.** If `V₁` (`n × k`) has orthonormal columns and `G` is an
`n × t` standard Gaussian matrix, then `V₁ᵀ G` is a `k × t` standard Gaussian matrix.

HMT 2011 (Halko–Martinsson–Tropp), §10.2 (with `G = Ω` and `V₁` the leading right singular
vectors: `Ω₁ = V₁ᵀ Ω` is standard Gaussian). Atlas: `block-law-indep`. Ported from the Prove2me
workspace, Gaussian Random Matrices series.

signature:
NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_map_first_cols (n : ℕ) {q t : ℕ} (hqt : q ≤ t) :
  MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun G i j => G i (Fin.castLE hqt j)) (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix n t) =
    NLAlib.gaussianMatrix n q
name: NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_map_first_cols
doc:
Selecting the first `q` columns of an `n×t` standard Gaussian matrix gives the
`n×q` standard Gaussian law. HMT 2011, §10.2; atlas `gaussian-matrix-def`,
`gn-expected-error` (rank-deficient first-sketch helper).

signature:
NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_map_inv_self_mul_transpose_apply_self {r k : ℕ} (hrk : r ≤ k) (i : Fin r) :
  MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun G => (Matrix.of G * (Matrix.of G).transpose)⁻¹ i i) (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix r k) =
    MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun x => (∑ j, x j ^ 2)⁻¹)
      (MeasureTheory.Measure.pi fun x => ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 1)
name: NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_map_inv_self_mul_transpose_apply_self
doc:
**Law of a diagonal entry of the inverse Wishart matrix.** For an `r × k` standard Gaussian
matrix `G` with `r ≤ k` and any `i`, `(G Gᵀ)⁻¹ᵢᵢ` has the law of `1/χ²_{k-r+1}`, i.e. of
`(∑ⱼ xⱼ²)⁻¹` for a standard Gaussian vector `x ∈ ℝ^{k-r+1}`.

HMT 2011, proof of Prop A.5 / Tropp–Webber 2023, proof of Lemma B.2 (each diagonal entry of an
inverse Wishart matrix is an inverse chi-square). Atlas: `pinv-frob-tail`,
`inverse-wishart-frob-moment` (helper). Proof: Schur complement
(`inv_self_mul_transpose_apply_self`), conditioning on the other rows, which have full rank
a.s. (`gaussianMatrix_ae_rank_eq`, atlas `gaussian-full-rank-ae`), and the residual law
(`pi_gaussianReal_map_sq_dist_rowSpace`, atlas `block-law-indep`). Ported from Prove2me
solution `GaussianMatrix.inverse_wishart_diag_law`.

signature:
NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_map_orthogonal {p m : ℕ} (U : Matrix (Fin p) (Fin p) ℝ) (V : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) ℝ)
  (hU : U.transpose * U = 1) (hV : V.transpose * V = 1) :
  MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun G => Matrix.of.symm (U * Matrix.of G * V)) (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix p m) =
    NLAlib.gaussianMatrix p m
name: NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_map_orthogonal
doc:
**Orthogonal invariance of the standard Gaussian matrix.** For orthogonal `U` (`p × p`) and
`V` (`m × m`), the law of `U G V` is the law of `G` when `G` is a `p × m` standard Gaussian
matrix.

HMT 2011 (Halko–Martinsson–Tropp), §10.1 (rotational invariance of the standard Gaussian
matrix). Atlas: `rotation-invariance`. The law is the pushforward of
`gaussianMatrix p m` (a measure on `Fin p → Fin m → ℝ`), so the map is written with
`Matrix.of.symm`. Ported from the Prove2me workspace, Gaussian Random Matrices series.

signature:
NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_map_sigmaMin_transpose_sq_Ioc_le_of_antitone_density {r k : ℕ} (hr : 1 ≤ r) (hrk : r ≤ k)
  (h : ℝ → ℝ) (hh : Measurable h) (hnn : ∀ y ∈ Set.Ioi 0, 0 ≤ h y) (hanti : AntitoneOn h (Set.Ioi 0))
  (hdens :
    (MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun G => NLAlib.sigmaMin (Matrix.of G).transpose ^ 2)
            (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix r k)).restrict
        (Set.Ioi 0) =
      (MeasureTheory.volume.restrict (Set.Ioi 0)).withDensity fun y =>
        ENNReal.ofReal (y ^ ((↑k - ↑r - 1) / 2) * Real.exp (-y / 2) * h y))
  (t : ℝ) :
  (MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun G => NLAlib.sigmaMin (Matrix.of G).transpose ^ 2) (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix r k))
      (Set.Ioc 0 t) ≤
    ∫⁻ (y : ℝ) in Set.Ioc 0 t,
      ENNReal.ofReal
        (2 ^ ((↑k - ↑r - 1) / 2) * Real.Gamma ((↑k + 1) / 2) / (Real.Gamma (↑r / 2) * Real.Gamma (↑k - ↑r + 1)) *
            y ^ ((↑k - ↑r - 1) / 2) *
          Real.exp (-y / 2))
name: NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_map_sigmaMin_transpose_sq_Ioc_le_of_antitone_density
doc:
An antitone Gamma-weighted density for the squared smallest Gaussian
singular value implies the exact Edelman CDF bound. Source: operator
rederivations Section 5; atlas `wishart-lambda-min-tail`. All moment and
endpoint hypotheses are discharged by the operator probe; only the scalar
density representation remains as the explicit input.

Flattening a standard Gaussian matrix gives i.i.d. standard Gaussians indexed by

signature:
NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_one_sigmaMin_transpose_sq_le_eq {k : ℕ} (hk : 1 ≤ k) (t : ℝ) (ht : 0 ≤ t) :
  (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix 1 k) {G | NLAlib.sigmaMin (Matrix.of G).transpose ^ 2 ≤ t} =
    ∫⁻ (x : ℝ) in Set.Ioc 0 t,
      ENNReal.ofReal
        (2 ^ ((↑k - 2) / 2) * Real.Gamma ((↑k + 1) / 2) / (Real.Gamma (1 / 2) * Real.Gamma ↑k) * x ^ ((↑k - 2) / 2) *
          Real.exp (-x / 2))
name: NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_one_sigmaMin_transpose_sq_le_eq
doc:
**The smallest Wishart eigenvalue for `r = 1`.** For a `1 × k` standard Gaussian matrix
`G` (`k ≥ 1`) and `t ≥ 0`, `σ_min(Gᵀ)² = ‖G‖² ∼ χ²_k`, and
`P[σ_min(Gᵀ)² ≤ t] = ∫₀ᵗ c(1,k) x^{(k-2)/2} e^{-x/2} dx` with
`c(1,k) = 2^{(k-2)/2} Γ((k+1)/2) / (Γ(1/2) Γ(k))` (`= 1/(2^{k/2} Γ(k/2))` by Legendre
duplication): the `χ²_k` CDF written in the shape of Tropp–Webber 2023, (B.5).

Tropp–Webber 2023, (B.5) in the case `r = 1` (where it is an equality); Edelman 1988.
Atlas: `wishart-lambda-min-tail` (sanity case). Proof: polar coordinates for the standard
Gaussian vector and the substitution `y = √x`. Ported from Prove2me solution
`GaussianMatrix.wishart_lambda_min_cdf_rank_one`.

signature:
NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_sigmaMin_transpose_sq_le_le {r k : ℕ} (hr : 1 ≤ r) (hrk : r ≤ k) (t : ℝ) (ht : 0 < t) :
  (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix r k) {G | NLAlib.sigmaMin (Matrix.of G).transpose ^ 2 ≤ t} ≤
    ENNReal.ofReal (1 / Real.Gamma (↑k - ↑r + 2) * (t * (↑k + ↑r) / 2) ^ ((↑k - ↑r + 1) / 2))
name: NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_sigmaMin_transpose_sq_le_le
doc:
**Lower tail of the smallest Wishart eigenvalue.** For an `r × k` standard Gaussian matrix
`G` with `1 ≤ r ≤ k` and `t > 0`,
`P[λ_min(G Gᵀ) ≤ t] = P[σ_min(Gᵀ)² ≤ t] ≤ (1/Γ(k-r+2)) (t (k+r)/2)^{(k-r+1)/2}`.

Tropp–Webber 2023, (B.7); Chen–Dongarra 2005, Lemma 4.1. Atlas: `wishart-lambda-min-tail`.
Proof: the density bound (B.5)
(`gaussianMatrix_sigmaMin_transpose_sq_le_le_lintegral`, proved here), the Gamma-ratio estimate
(`gammaRatio_le`) and `∫₀ᵗ x^a e^{-x/2} dx ≤ t^{a+1}/(a+1)` (`lintegral_rpow_mul_exp_le`, atlas
`tail-integral`). Ported from Prove2me solution `GaussianMatrix.wishart_lambda_min_tail`.

signature:
NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_sigmaMin_transpose_sq_le_le_lintegral {r k : ℕ} (hr : 1 ≤ r) (hrk : r ≤ k) (t : ℝ) (ht : 0 < t) :
  (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix r k) {G | NLAlib.sigmaMin (Matrix.of G).transpose ^ 2 ≤ t} ≤
    ∫⁻ (x : ℝ) in Set.Ioc 0 t,
      ENNReal.ofReal
        (2 ^ ((↑k - ↑r - 1) / 2) * Real.Gamma ((↑k + 1) / 2) / (Real.Gamma (↑r / 2) * Real.Gamma (↑k - ↑r + 1)) *
            x ^ ((↑k - ↑r - 1) / 2) *
          Real.exp (-x / 2))
name: NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_sigmaMin_transpose_sq_le_le_lintegral
doc:
**Density bound for the smallest Wishart eigenvalue** (Tropp–Webber 2023, (B.5); Edelman
1988, Chen–Dongarra 2005). For an `r × k` standard Gaussian matrix `G` with `1 ≤ r ≤ k` and
`t > 0`,
`P[σ_min(Gᵀ)² ≤ t] ≤ ∫₀ᵗ c(r,k) x^{(k-r-1)/2} e^{-x/2} dx` with
`c(r,k) = 2^{(k-r-1)/2} Γ((k+1)/2) / (Γ(r/2) Γ(k-r+1))`.

Atlas: `wishart-lambda-min-tail`. Proof: Gaussian operator calculus gives a scalar
weak inequality; the scalar weighted-density theorem and quadratic-probe Mellin
endpoint recover the exact coefficient. No joint Wishart eigenvalue density or
Vandermonde Jacobian is used. The rank-one case holds with equality. The statement
is identical to the Prove2me density-bound theorem.

signature:

  (hLip : ∀ (X Y : Fin p → Fin m → ℝ), |h X - h Y| ≤ L * NLAlib.frobNorm (Matrix.of X - Matrix.of Y)) (t : ℝ)
  (ht : 0 ≤ t) :
  MeasureTheory.Integrable h (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix p m) ∧

doc:
**Gaussian concentration for Lipschitz functions of a Gaussian matrix**: for
`h` on `p × m` arrays that is `L`-Lipschitz in the Frobenius norm (`L > 0`) and `t ≥ 0`, `h` is

signature:

doc:
**Gaussian concentration** for Lipschitz functions of a standard Gaussian vector: for `f`
`L`-Lipschitz (Euclidean, `L > 0`) on `ι → ℝ` and `t ≥ 0`, `f` is `γₙ`-integrable and
`γₙ{x | 𝔼 f + L t ≤ f x} ≤ e^{-t²/2}`.

Boucheron–Lugosi–Massart 2013, Thm 5.6; Vershynin 2012, Prop 5.34. Atlas:
`gaussian-concentration`. Ported from Prove2me solution
`GaussianMatrix.gaussian_concentration_vector`.

name: NLAlib.isSubspaceEmbedding_iff_of_hasOrthonormalCols
doc:
Orthonormal form of a subspace embedding (Woodruff 2014 §2.1; Martinsson–Tropp 2020 §8.7):
for `U` with orthonormal columns, `S` is an `ε`-subspace embedding for `range U` iff
`(1 - ε)‖x‖² ≤ ‖SUx‖² ≤ (1 + ε)‖x‖²` for every coefficient vector `x`.

Atlas: `ose-def`.

signature:
NLAlib.isSubspaceEmbedding_iff_singularValues {k m d : ℕ} {S : Matrix (Fin k) (Fin m) ℝ} {U : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin d) ℝ}
  (hU : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols U) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 ≤ ε) (hε1 : ε ≤ 1) :
  NLAlib.IsSubspaceEmbedding S U ε ↔
    ∀ (j : Fin d), √(1 - ε) ≤ NLAlib.singularValues (S * U) ↑j ∧ NLAlib.singularValues (S * U) ↑j ≤ √(1 + ε)
name: NLAlib.isSubspaceEmbedding_iff_singularValues
doc:
Complete singular-value OSE equivalence for `0 ≤ ε ≤ 1`: the sketch
preserves the subspace iff every domain singular value of `S U` lies in
`[√(1−ε), √(1+ε)]`. Atlas: `ose-def`, `svd`. Includes empty dimensions.

signature:
NLAlib.isSubspaceEmbedding_iff_singularValues_fintype.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {p : Type u_3}
  [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [Fintype p] [DecidableEq n] {S : Matrix p m ℝ} {U : Matrix m n ℝ}
  (hU : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols U) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 ≤ ε) (hε1 : ε ≤ 1) :
  NLAlib.IsSubspaceEmbedding S U ε ↔
    ∀ (j : Fin (Fintype.card n)),
      √(1 - ε) ≤ NLAlib.singularValues ((Matrix.reindex (Fintype.equivFin p) (Fintype.equivFin n)) (S * U)) ↑j ∧
        NLAlib.singularValues ((Matrix.reindex (Fintype.equivFin p) (Fintype.equivFin n)) (S * U)) ↑j ≤ √(1 + ε)
name: NLAlib.isSubspaceEmbedding_iff_singularValues_fintype
doc:
Complete OSE singular-value criterion on arbitrary finite indices.
For `0 ≤ ε ≤ 1`, every domain singular value of the normalized `S U` lies in
`[√(1−ε), √(1+ε)]` precisely when `S` embeds the frame's subspace.
Atlas `ose-def`, `svd`; the list uses explicit `Fin(card)` normalization.

name: NLAlib.isSubspaceEmbedding_iff_specNorm_transpose_mul_self_sub_one_le
doc:
Complete Gram-form equivalence for an orthonormal frame, valid also in
empty dimensions. Atlas: `ose-def`.

name: NLAlib.isSubspaceEmbedding_mul_right_iff
doc:
Basis independence (Woodruff 2014 §2.1): for invertible `C`, `S` is an `ε`-subspace
embedding for `range U` iff it is one for `range (U C)`. The property depends on the subspace
only.

Atlas: `ose-def`.

name: NLAlib.isSubspaceEmbedding_of_specNorm_transpose_mul_self_sub_one_le
doc:
Gram form of a subspace embedding (Woodruff 2014 §2.1; Martinsson–Tropp 2020 §8.7), the
direction used in practice: for `U` with orthonormal columns, `‖(SU)ᵀ(SU) − I‖₂ ≤ ε` implies
that `S` is an `ε`-subspace embedding for `range U`. (The converse also holds; not yet
formalized.)

Atlas: `ose-def`.

signature:
NLAlib.isometry_reflection_identities.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {κ : Type u_2} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype κ]
  [DecidableEq κ] (K : Matrix ι κ ℂ) (hK : K.conjTranspose * K = 1) (A : Matrix ι ι ℂ) (B : Matrix κ κ ℂ) :
  have U := Matrix.fromBlocks (1 - K * K.conjTranspose) K K.conjTranspose 0;
  U.IsHermitian ∧ U * U = 1 ∧ (U * Matrix.fromBlocks A 0 0 B * U).toBlocks₂₂ = K.conjTranspose * A * K
name: NLAlib.isometry_reflection_identities
doc:
For an isometry `K`, the block matrix `U = fromBlocks (1 - K Kᴴ) K Kᴴ 0` is a Hermitian involution
and the lower-right block of `U (fromBlocks A 0 0 B) U` is `Kᴴ A K`.

Tropp 2015, proof of Thm 8.5.2 (unitary dilation). Atlas: `operator-monotone-convex`. Ported from
the Prove2me mission *An Introduction to Matrix Concentration Inequalities, Ch 8*.

Auxiliary; not a numbered result in the source.

signature:
NLAlib.jl_distributional (k n : ℕ) (x : Fin n → ℝ) {ε : ℝ} (hε0 : 0 < ε) (hε1 : ε < 1) :
  (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix k n)
      {G | |((1 / √↑k) • Matrix.of G).mulVec x ⬝ᵥ ((1 / √↑k) • Matrix.of G).mulVec x - x ⬝ᵥ x| > ε * x ⬝ᵥ x} ≤
    ENNReal.ofReal (2 * Real.exp (-↑k * (ε ^ 2 / 4 - ε ^ 3 / 6)))
name: NLAlib.jl_distributional
doc:
SCAFFOLD: jl-distributional.

Distributional Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma for the Gaussian sketch (Dasgupta–Gupta 2003,
Lem 2.2; Woodruff 2014 §2.1): for `S = k^{-1/2} G` with `G` standard Gaussian `k × n`, any fixed
`x : ℝⁿ` and `0 < ε < 1`,
`P[|‖Sx‖² − ‖x‖²| > ε‖x‖²] ≤ 2 exp(−k(ε²/4 − ε³/6))`.

Deferred: the proof needs rotation invariance of the Gaussian matrix (`‖Gx‖² / ‖x‖²` is
`χ²_k`) and the two Chernoff tails of the chi-square law (atlas `rotation-invariance`,
`chi-square-upper-tail`, `chi-square-lower-tail`), none of which is yet in the library.

signature:
NLAlib.jl_lemma (k n N : ℕ) (p : Fin N → Fin n → ℝ) {ε : ℝ} (hε0 : 0 < ε) (hε1 : ε < 1) :
  (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix k n)
      {G |
        ∃ i j,
          i ≠ j ∧
            |((1 / √↑k) • Matrix.of G).mulVec (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ ((1 / √↑k) • Matrix.of G).mulVec (p i - p j) -
                  (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ (p i - p j)| >
              ε * (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ (p i - p j)} ≤
    ENNReal.ofReal (↑N ^ 2 * 2 * Real.exp (-↑k * (ε ^ 2 / 4 - ε ^ 3 / 6)))
name: NLAlib.jl_lemma
doc:
Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma, union-bound form (Dasgupta–Gupta 2003, Thm 2.1): for a finite
family `p : Fin N → ℝⁿ`, the probability that the Gaussian sketch `S = k^{-1/2} G` distorts some
pairwise squared distance `‖p i − p j‖²` by more than a factor `1 ± ε` is at most
`N² · 2 exp(−k(ε²/4 − ε³/6))`.

Deviation: the union is taken over all `N²` ordered pairs (not the `N(N−1)/2` unordered ones),
which costs a constant factor `2` in the bound. No measurability hypothesis is needed (the union
bound holds for the outer measure).

Atlas: `jl-lemma`; uses `jl-distributional`.

signature:
NLAlib.jl_lemma_exists (k n N : ℕ) (p : Fin N → Fin n → ℝ) {ε : ℝ} (hε0 : 0 < ε) (hε1 : ε < 1) (hN : 2 ≤ N)
  (hk : 48 * Real.log ↑N / ε ^ 2 ≤ ↑k) :
  ∃ S,
    ∀ (i j : Fin N),
      (1 - ε) * (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ (p i - p j) ≤ S.mulVec (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ S.mulVec (p i - p j) ∧
        S.mulVec (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ S.mulVec (p i - p j) ≤ (1 + ε) * (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ (p i - p j)
name: NLAlib.jl_lemma_exists
doc:
Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma, existence form (Johnson–Lindenstrauss 1984; Dasgupta–Gupta
2003, Thm 2.1): any `N ≥ 2` points of `ℝⁿ` admit a linear map `S : ℝⁿ → ℝᵏ` with
`k ≥ 48 log N / ε²` that preserves every pairwise squared distance to within `1 ± ε`.

Atlas: `jl-lemma`; uses `jl-distributional`.

signature:
NLAlib.jl_lemma_prob_le_half (k n N : ℕ) (p : Fin N → Fin n → ℝ) {ε : ℝ} (hε0 : 0 < ε) (hε1 : ε < 1) (hN : 2 ≤ N)
  (hk : 48 * Real.log ↑N / ε ^ 2 ≤ ↑k) :
  (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix k n)
      {G |
        ∃ i j,
          i ≠ j ∧
            |((1 / √↑k) • Matrix.of G).mulVec (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ ((1 / √↑k) • Matrix.of G).mulVec (p i - p j) -
                  (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ (p i - p j)| >
              ε * (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ (p i - p j)} ≤
    ENNReal.ofReal (1 / 2)
name: NLAlib.jl_lemma_prob_le_half
doc:
Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma, `O(ε⁻² log N)` form (Dasgupta–Gupta 2003, Thm 2.1): for
`N ≥ 2` points, `0 < ε < 1` and `k ≥ 48 log N / ε²`, the Gaussian sketch `S = k^{-1/2} G`
distorts some pairwise squared distance by more than `1 ± ε` with probability at most `1/2`.

Deviation: the explicit constant `48` (from `(ε²/4 − ε³/6)⁻¹ ≤ 12/ε²` and
`log(4N²) ≤ 4 log N` for `N ≥ 2`) is not optimised; Dasgupta–Gupta's constant is `4·(1/2 − ε/3)⁻¹`
at failure probability `1 − 1/N`.

Atlas: `jl-lemma`; uses `jl-distributional`.

signature:
NLAlib.jl_lemma_prob_le_of_log_le (k n N : ℕ) (p : Fin N → Fin n → ℝ) {ε δ : ℝ} (hε0 : 0 < ε) (hε1 : ε < 1) (hδ : 0 < δ)
  (hk : (ε ^ 2 / 4 - ε ^ 3 / 6)⁻¹ * Real.log (2 * ↑N ^ 2 / δ) ≤ ↑k) :
  (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix k n)
      {G |
        ∃ i j,
          i ≠ j ∧
            |((1 / √↑k) • Matrix.of G).mulVec (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ ((1 / √↑k) • Matrix.of G).mulVec (p i - p j) -
                  (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ (p i - p j)| >
              ε * (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ (p i - p j)} ≤
    ENNReal.ofReal δ
name: NLAlib.jl_lemma_prob_le_of_log_le
doc:
Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma with explicit dimension (Dasgupta–Gupta 2003, Thm 2.1): if
`0 < ε < 1`, `0 < δ` and `k ≥ (ε²/4 − ε³/6)⁻¹ log(2N²/δ)`, then with probability at least
`1 − δ` the Gaussian sketch `S = k^{-1/2} G` preserves all pairwise squared distances of
`p : Fin N → ℝⁿ` to within `1 ± ε`.

Deviation: Dasgupta–Gupta take `k ≥ 4 (ε²/2 − ε³/3)⁻¹ log N`, aiming at success probability
`1/N`; we state the general-`δ` form with the constant coming from the ordered-pair union bound
in `jl_lemma`.

Atlas: `jl-lemma`; uses `jl-distributional`.

signature: NLAlib.matrixMeasurableSpace.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} : MeasurableSpace (Matrix m n ℂ)
name: NLAlib.matrixMeasurableSpace
doc:
The Borel σ-algebra on complex matrices (for the norm topology), used to state measurability of
random matrices.

This global instance is a deliberate exception to STANDARDS §3, which states measurability of
matrix-valued maps entrywise because Mathlib has no `MeasurableSpace (Matrix m n ℂ)`. The matrix
concentration development (ported from the Tropp 2015 Prove2me missions) treats random matrices as
`Measurable` maps into a normed space and integrates them as Bochner integrals in the operator
norm; every statement in `NLAlib/Concentration/Matrix/` that mentions `Measurable`, `iIndepFun` or
`Integrable` for a matrix-valued map elaborates through this instance, so removing it would mean
restating the whole development. Mathlib declares no competing instance (`Matrix` is a
non-reducible `def`, so the product σ-algebra on `m → n → ℂ` is not found), hence no diamond. It
could be made `scoped`: checked 2026-10-09, wrapping it in `namespace MatrixBorel` as a `scoped
instance` and adding `open scoped NLAlib.MatrixBorel` to the 35 modules under
`Concentration/Matrix/` that import this one (directly or not) builds cleanly, at the price of
every downstream user opening the scope to state the hypotheses of the public theorems.

signature:
NLAlib.matrix_bernstein.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω)
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {m n N : ℕ} [NeZero m] [NeZero n] (S : Fin N → Ω → Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℂ)
  (L : ℝ) (hL : 0 ≤ L) (hMeas : ∀ (k : Fin N), Measurable (S k)) (hIndep : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun S μ)
  (hMean : ∀ (k : Fin N), ∫ (ω : Ω), S k ω ∂μ = 0)
  (hBound : ∀ (k : Fin N), ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, NLAlib.spectralNorm (S k ω) ≤ L) :
  have Z := fun ω => ∑ k, S k ω;
  have v := NLAlib.rectSecondMoment μ Z;
  v =
      max (NLAlib.spectralNorm (∑ k, ∫ (ω : Ω), S k ω * (S k ω).conjTranspose ∂μ))
        (NLAlib.spectralNorm (∑ k, ∫ (ω : Ω), (S k ω).conjTranspose * S k ω ∂μ)) ∧
    ∫ (ω : Ω), NLAlib.spectralNorm (Z ω) ∂μ ≤ √(2 * v * Real.log (↑m + ↑n)) + L * Real.log (↑m + ↑n) / 3 ∧
      ∀ (t : ℝ), 0 ≤ t → (μ {ω | t ≤ NLAlib.spectralNorm (Z ω)}).toReal ≤ NLAlib.bernsteinTail (m + n) v L t
name: NLAlib.matrix_bernstein
doc:
Matrix Bernstein inequality, rectangular case: for an independent sum `Z` of centered random `m ×
n` matrices with `‖S k‖ ≤ L`, `𝔼 ‖Z‖ ≤ √(2 v log (m + n)) + L log (m + n) / 3` and `P{‖Z‖ ≥ t} ≤
bernsteinTail (m + n) v L t`.

Tropp 2015, Thm 6.1.1. Atlas: `matrix-bernstein`. Ported from the Prove2me mission *An
Introduction to Matrix Concentration Inequalities, Ch 6*.

signature:
NLAlib.matrix_chernoff.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω)
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {d N : ℕ} [NeZero d] (X : Fin N → Ω → Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℂ) (L : ℝ)
  (hL : 0 ≤ L) (hMeas : ∀ (k : Fin N), Measurable (X k)) (hIndep : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun X μ)
  (hHerm : ∀ (k : Fin N), ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, (X k ω).IsHermitian)
  (hBound : ∀ (k : Fin N), ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, 0 ≤ NLAlib.lambdaMin (X k ω) ∧ NLAlib.lambdaMax (X k ω) ≤ L) :
  have Y := fun ω => ∑ k, X k ω;
  have a := NLAlib.lambdaMin (∫ (ω : Ω), Y ω ∂μ);
  have b := NLAlib.lambdaMax (∫ (ω : Ω), Y ω ∂μ);
  a = NLAlib.lambdaMin (∑ k, ∫ (ω : Ω), X k ω ∂μ) ∧
    b = NLAlib.lambdaMax (∑ k, ∫ (ω : Ω), X k ω ∂μ) ∧
      (∀ (θ : ℝ),
          0 < θ →
            (1 - Real.exp (-θ)) / θ * a - L * Real.log ↑d / θ ≤ ∫ (ω : Ω), NLAlib.lambdaMin (Y ω) ∂μ ∧
              ∫ (ω : Ω), NLAlib.lambdaMax (Y ω) ∂μ ≤ (Real.exp θ - 1) / θ * b + L * Real.log ↑d / θ) ∧
        (∀ (ε : ℝ),
            0 ≤ ε → ε < 1 → (μ {ω | NLAlib.lambdaMin (Y ω) ≤ (1 - ε) * a}).toReal ≤ NLAlib.chernoffLowerTail d a L ε) ∧
          ∀ (ε : ℝ), 0 ≤ ε → (μ {ω | (1 + ε) * b ≤ NLAlib.lambdaMax (Y ω)}).toReal ≤ NLAlib.chernoffUpperTail d b L ε
name: NLAlib.matrix_chernoff
doc:
Matrix Chernoff inequality: for an independent sum of random positive semidefinite matrices with
`λmax ≤ L`, expectation bounds on `λmin` and `λmax` for every `θ > 0` and the lower and upper
tails `chernoffLowerTail`, `chernoffUpperTail`.

Tropp 2015, Thm 5.1.1, eqs (5.1.1–6). Atlas: `matrix-chernoff`. Ported from the Prove2me mission
*An Introduction to Matrix Concentration Inequalities, Ch 5*.

The expectation bounds are stated for every `θ > 0` before optimisation; degenerate `L = 0`
follows the piecewise tail definitions.

signature:

  (g : Fin N → Ω → ℝ) (hMeas : ∀ (k : Fin N), Measurable (g k)) (hIndep : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun g μ)

  have Z := fun ω => ∑ k, g k ω • B k;
  have v := NLAlib.rectSecondMoment μ Z;
  v =
      max (NLAlib.spectralNorm (∑ k, B k * (B k).conjTranspose))
        (NLAlib.spectralNorm (∑ k, (B k).conjTranspose * B k)) ∧
    ∫ (ω : Ω), NLAlib.spectralNorm (Z ω) ∂μ ≤ √(2 * v * Real.log (↑m + ↑n)) ∧

gaussianSeriesTail (m + n) v t`.

Tropp 2015, Thm 4.1.1. Atlas: `matrix-gaussian-series`. Ported from the Prove2me mission *An
Introduction to Matrix Concentration Inequalities, Ch 4*.

doc:

`N × n` standard Gaussian matrix `A` with `1 ≤ n ≤ N` and `n s² ≤ N - n + 1`,
`P(σ_min(A) ≤ s) ≤ n · (e n s² / (N - n + 1))^{(N - n + 1)/2}`. The source's hypothesis

Rudelson–Vershynin 2009 (sharper `(C s √N)^{N-n+1}` form). Union bound over the columns of the
column-distance estimate. Atlas: `smin-small-ball`. Ported from Prove2me solution
`GaussianMatrix.sMin_small_ball`.

NLAlib.measure_sq_dist_colSpace_le_le_gaussianReal {N p d : ℕ} (B : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin p) ℝ) (hd : 1 ≤ d)

    ENNReal.ofReal ((Real.exp 1 * u / ↑d) ^ (↑d / 2))
name: NLAlib.measure_sq_dist_colSpace_le_le_gaussianReal
doc:
**Small ball for the distance to a subspace.** Let `B : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin p) ℝ` have
`rank B + d ≤ N` with `d ≥ 1`. For a standard Gaussian vector `g ∈ ℝᴺ` and `0 ≤ u ≤ d`,
`P(dist(g, range B)² ≤ u) ≤ (e u / d)^{d/2}`, with `dist(g, range B) = inf_c ‖g - B c‖₂`.

The squared distance dominates the sum of squares of `d` coordinates of `g` in an orthonormal
basis of `(range B)ᗮ` (Bessel), which is `χ²_d` by rotation invariance; then the chi-square lower
tail. Davidson–Szarek 2001, proof of Thm II.13; Vershynin 2012, §5.2.
Atlas: `smin-small-ball` (step). Ported from Prove2me solution
`GaussianMatrix.gaussian_dist_colspace_small_ball`.

  (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix N n) {A | (⨅ x, √((Matrix.of A).mulVec ↑x ⬝ᵥ (Matrix.of A).mulVec ↑x)) ^ 2 ≤ u} ≤

name: NLAlib.measure_sq_dist_col_span_le_le_gaussianMatrix
doc:
**Small ball for the distance from a column to the span of the others.** For an `N × n`
standard Gaussian matrix `A` with `n ≤ N`, any column `j` and `0 ≤ u ≤ N - n + 1`,
`P(dist(A_j, span{A_l : l ≠ j})² ≤ u) ≤ (e u / (N - n + 1))^{(N - n + 1)/2}`, the distance
being written `inf { ‖A x‖₂ : x_j = 1 }`.

Condition on the other columns (resample column `j`) and apply the subspace small-ball bound
with `d = N - n + 1`. Davidson–Szarek 2001, proof of Thm II.13; Vershynin 2012, §5.2.
Atlas: `smin-small-ball` (step). Ported from Prove2me solution
`GaussianMatrix.dist_col_span_small_ball`.

signature:

`1 ≤ p ≤ 18` and `x ≥ 2p`,

Atlas: `extreme-singular-values-deviation`. Ported from Prove2me solution
`GaussianMatrix.extreme_singular_values_deviation`.

(`frobSq_residual_le_of_range_subset`, i.e.

**Randomized SVD with a Gaussian test matrix** (Chen–Persson, Theorem `thm:RSVD`, Algorithm
RSVD; HMT 2011, Thm 10.5, Frobenius case): if `Ω` is an `n × t` standard Gaussian matrix,
`t ≥ k + 2`, and `Q ω` has a.s. orthonormal columns with `range(AΩ) ⊆ range(Q)`, then
`E‖A − QQᵀA‖_F² ≤ (1 + k/(t−k−1)) ‖A − ⟦A⟧ₖ‖_F²` (`‖A − ⟦A⟧ₖ‖_F² = frobSq S₂` via the block SVD).
`rsvd_main` with its Gaussian hypotheses `hunit`, `hinv`, `hZi` discharged. The integrability
hypothesis `hXi` is also removed: when the error is not integrable its Bochner integral is `0`
and the (nonnegative) bound holds trivially. No measurability of `Q` is required.
Deviation: `n`, `k`, `r`, `r'`, `t` are `Fin` (the Gaussian law of `Ω` and the block lemmas of
`Gaussian/Conditioning.lean` live on `Fin`); the row type `m` and the column type `q` of `Q`
are arbitrary.

`gaussian-full-rank-ae`, `hmt-9-1-frobenius`).

  {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ωs} {m : Type u_2} {n : Type u_3} {r : Type u_4} {r' : Type u_5} {q : Type u_6} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [Fintype r] [Fintype r'] [Fintype q] [DecidableEq r] [DecidableEq r'] [DecidableEq q] {k t : ℕ}
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {A : Matrix m n ℝ} {U₁ : Matrix m (Fin k) ℝ} {U₂ : Matrix m r ℝ}
  {V₁ : Matrix n (Fin k) ℝ} {V₂ : Matrix n r' ℝ} {S₁ : Matrix (Fin k) (Fin k) ℝ} {S₂ : Matrix r r' ℝ}
  (hA : A = U₁ * S₁ * V₁.transpose + U₂ * S₂ * V₂.transpose) (hU₂ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols U₂)
  (hV₁ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols V₁) (hV₂ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols V₂) (hV : V₁.transpose * V₂ = 0)
  (hkt : k + 2 ≤ t) (Ω : Ωs → Matrix n (Fin t) ℝ) (Q : Ωs → Matrix m q ℝ) (Y : Ωs → Matrix q n ℝ)
  (hQo : ∀ᵐ (ω : Ωs) ∂μ, NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols (Q ω))
  (hQr : ∀ᵐ (ω : Ωs) ∂μ, Q ω * ((Q ω).transpose * (A * Ω ω)) = A * Ω ω)
  (hY : ∀ (ω : Ωs), NLAlib.IsBestRankApprox k ((Q ω).transpose * A) (Y ω))
  (hunit : ∀ᵐ (ω : Ωs) ∂μ, IsUnit (V₁.transpose * Ω ω * (V₁.transpose * Ω ω).transpose))
  (hinv :
    ∫ (ω : Ωs), NLAlib.frobSq (S₂ * (V₂.transpose * Ω ω) * NLAlib.pinvR (V₁.transpose * Ω ω)) ∂μ =
      ↑k / (↑t - ↑k - 1) * NLAlib.frobSq S₂)
  (hXi : MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun ω => NLAlib.frobSq (A - Q ω * Y ω)) μ)
  (hZi :
    MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun ω => NLAlib.frobSq (S₂ * (V₂.transpose * Ω ω) * NLAlib.pinvR (V₁.transpose * Ω ω)))
      μ) :
  ∫ (ω : Ωs), NLAlib.frobSq (A - Q ω * Y ω) ∂μ ≤ (1 + ↑k / (↑t - ↑k - 1)) * NLAlib.frobSq S₂
name: NLAlib.rsvd_truncated_main

signature:
NLAlib.rsvd_truncated_main_gaussian.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {Ωs : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ωs] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ωs}
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {m : Type u_2} {q : Type u_3} [Fintype m] [Fintype q] [DecidableEq q]
  {n k r r' t : ℕ} {A : Matrix m (Fin n) ℝ} {U₁ : Matrix m (Fin k) ℝ} {U₂ : Matrix m (Fin r) ℝ}
  {V₁ : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin k) ℝ} {V₂ : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin r') ℝ} {S₁ : Matrix (Fin k) (Fin k) ℝ}
  {S₂ : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r') ℝ} (hA : A = U₁ * S₁ * V₁.transpose + U₂ * S₂ * V₂.transpose)
  (hU₂ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols U₂) (hV₁ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols V₁) (hV₂ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols V₂)
  (hV : V₁.transpose * V₂ = 0) (hkt : k + 2 ≤ t) (Ω : Ωs → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin t) ℝ)
  (hΩ : MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun ω => Matrix.of.symm (Ω ω)) μ = NLAlib.gaussianMatrix n t) (Q : Ωs → Matrix m q ℝ)
  (Y : Ωs → Matrix q (Fin n) ℝ) (hQo : ∀ᵐ (ω : Ωs) ∂μ, NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols (Q ω))
  (hQr : ∀ᵐ (ω : Ωs) ∂μ, Q ω * ((Q ω).transpose * (A * Ω ω)) = A * Ω ω)
  (hY : ∀ (ω : Ωs), NLAlib.IsBestRankApprox k ((Q ω).transpose * A) (Y ω)) :
  ∫ (ω : Ωs), NLAlib.frobSq (A - Q ω * Y ω) ∂μ ≤ (1 + ↑k / (↑t - ↑k - 1)) * NLAlib.frobSq S₂
name: NLAlib.rsvd_truncated_main_gaussian
doc:
**Truncated randomized SVD with a Gaussian test matrix** (Chen–Persson, Theorem `thm:RSVD`,
Algorithm tRSVD, output `Q⟦QᵀA⟧ₖ`; HMT 2011, Thm 10.5): as `rsvd_main_gaussian`, with
`Y ω` any best rank-`k` approximation of `Q ωᵀ A`:
`E‖A − Q⟦QᵀA⟧ₖ‖_F² ≤ (1 + k/(t−k−1)) ‖A − ⟦A⟧ₖ‖_F²`. No Gaussian or integrability hypothesis
remains. Atlas `rsvd-expected-error` (uses `gaussian-conditioning`, `pinv-frob-moment`,
`gaussian-full-rank-ae`, `hmt-9-1-frobenius`).

signature:
NLAlib.self_mem_krylovSpace_succ.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (b : n → ℝ)
  (q : ℕ) : b ∈ NLAlib.krylovSpace A b (q + 1)
name: NLAlib.self_mem_krylovSpace_succ
doc:
The starting vector lies in every nontrivial Krylov space: `b ∈ K_{q+1}(A,b)`.
Source: [`gm10`], Ch. 4. Atlas: `krylov-subspace`.

signature: NLAlib.sigmaMin.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.sigmaMin
doc:
The smallest singular value of a tall matrix `A : Matrix m n ℝ`:
`σ_min(A) = inf { ‖A x‖₂ : x ∈ ℝⁿ, ‖x‖₂ = 1 }` (`0` when `n` is empty, by the real convention
`inf ∅ = 0`). For a wide matrix use `sigmaMin Aᵀ`. Same definition as the Prove2me
`GaussianMatrix.sMin`.

signature: NLAlib.sigmaMinSq.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.sigmaMinSq
doc:
The squared smallest singular value of a tall matrix, `σ_min(A)² = λ_min(AᵀA)`
(`sigmaMinSq_eq_sigmaMin_sq`). For a wide matrix `G`, `sigmaMinSq Gᵀ = lamMin (G Gᵀ)`.

signature:
NLAlib.sigmaMinSq_eq_sigmaMin_sq.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) :
  NLAlib.sigmaMinSq A = NLAlib.sigmaMin A ^ 2
name: NLAlib.sigmaMinSq_eq_sigmaMin_sq
doc: `λ_min(AᵀA) = σ_min(A)²`. Atlas `norm-lipschitz`.

signature:
NLAlib.sigmaMinSq_nonneg.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) :
  0 ≤ NLAlib.sigmaMinSq A
name: NLAlib.sigmaMinSq_nonneg
doc: `λ_min(AᵀA) ≥ 0`. Atlas `norm-lipschitz`.

signature:
NLAlib.sigmaMin_eq_singularValues_last {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) (hn : 0 < n) :
  NLAlib.sigmaMin A = NLAlib.singularValues A (n - 1)
name: NLAlib.sigmaMin_eq_singularValues_last
doc:
The variational smallest singular value equals the last singular value
in the list indexed by the domain dimension. For wide matrices this list
includes kernel zeros; for tall matrices it is the usual smallest singular
value. Atlas: `svd`, `norm-lipschitz`. The empty-domain value is handled by
the existing theorem `sigmaMin_of_isEmpty`.

signature:
NLAlib.sigmaMin_eq_sqrt_sigmaMinSq.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) :
  NLAlib.sigmaMin A = √(NLAlib.sigmaMinSq A)
name: NLAlib.sigmaMin_eq_sqrt_sigmaMinSq
doc: `σ_min(A) = √(λ_min(AᵀA))`. Atlas `norm-lipschitz`.

signature:
NLAlib.sigmaMin_le_sigmaMin_add_frobNorm.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  (A B : Matrix m n ℝ) : NLAlib.sigmaMin A ≤ NLAlib.sigmaMin B + NLAlib.frobNorm (A - B)
name: NLAlib.sigmaMin_le_sigmaMin_add_frobNorm
doc:
One half of the Lipschitz bound: `σ_min(A) ≤ σ_min(B) + ‖A - B‖_F`.
Ported from Prove2me solution `GaussianMatrix.sMin_lipschitz` (helper
`sMin_le_sMin_add_frobNorm`). Atlas `norm-lipschitz`.

signature:
NLAlib.sigmaMin_le_sigmaMin_add_specNorm.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] (A B : Matrix m n ℝ) : NLAlib.sigmaMin A ≤ NLAlib.sigmaMin B + NLAlib.specNorm (A - B)
name: NLAlib.sigmaMin_le_sigmaMin_add_specNorm
doc:
One-sided Weyl perturbation bound in the spectral norm, including empty
dimensions. Atlas: `norm-lipschitz`.

signature:
NLAlib.sigmaMin_le_specNorm.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m]
  [DecidableEq n] [Nonempty n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) : NLAlib.sigmaMin A ≤ NLAlib.specNorm A
name: NLAlib.sigmaMin_le_specNorm
doc:
For a nonempty index type, the smallest singular value is at most the spectral norm.
Ported from the Prove2me solution `GaussianMatrix.gordon` (helper `gordonSol_sMin_le_specNorm`).
Atlas `norm-lipschitz`.

signature:
NLAlib.sigmaMin_le_sqrt_mulVec.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ)

name: NLAlib.sigmaMin_le_sqrt_mulVec
doc: `σ_min(A) ≤ ‖Ax‖₂` for every unit vector `x`. Atlas `norm-lipschitz`.

signature:
NLAlib.sigmaMin_mul_sqrt_le.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ)
  (x : n → ℝ) : NLAlib.sigmaMin A * √(x ⬝ᵥ x) ≤ √(A.mulVec x ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec x)
name: NLAlib.sigmaMin_mul_sqrt_le
doc: `σ_min(A) ‖x‖₂ ≤ ‖Ax‖₂` for every vector `x`. Atlas `norm-lipschitz`.

signature:
NLAlib.sigmaMin_nonneg.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) :

name: NLAlib.sigmaMin_nonneg
doc: `σ_min(A) ≥ 0`. Atlas `norm-lipschitz`.

signature:
NLAlib.sigmaMin_of_isEmpty.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [Fintype m] [IsEmpty n]
  (A : Matrix m n ℝ) : NLAlib.sigmaMin A = 0
name: NLAlib.sigmaMin_of_isEmpty
doc: On an empty index type the unit sphere is empty and `σ_min = 0`.

signature:
NLAlib.sigmaMin_pos_iff_rank_eq_width {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) (hn : 0 < n) :
  0 < NLAlib.sigmaMin A ↔ A.rank = n
name: NLAlib.sigmaMin_pos_iff_rank_eq_width
doc:
Positivity of the variational smallest singular value is exactly full
column rank when there is at least one column. Atlas: `svd`,
`randomized-kaczmarz`, `norm-lipschitz`.

signature:
NLAlib.sigmaMin_transpose_eq_zero_of_not_posDef_gram.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {κ : Type u_2} [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ]
  [DecidableEq ι] (G : Matrix ι κ ℝ) (hnot : ¬(G * G.transpose).PosDef) : NLAlib.sigmaMin G.transpose = 0
name: NLAlib.sigmaMin_transpose_eq_zero_of_not_posDef_gram

signature:
NLAlib.sigmaMin_transpose_sq.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (G : Matrix m n ℝ) :
  NLAlib.sigmaMin G.transpose ^ 2 = NLAlib.lamMin (G * G.transpose)
name: NLAlib.sigmaMin_transpose_sq
doc: For a wide matrix `G`, `σ_min(Gᵀ)² = λ_min(G Gᵀ)`. Atlas `norm-lipschitz`.

signature:
NLAlib.sigmaMin_transpose_sq_eq_inv_inverse_eigenvalue_sub.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
  {κ : Type u_2} [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ] (ε : ℝ) (G : Matrix ι κ ℝ) (hpd : (NLAlib.regularizedGram ε G).PosDef)

name: NLAlib.sigmaMin_transpose_sq_eq_inv_inverse_eigenvalue_sub
doc:
The maximal inverse regularized-Gram eigenvalue identifies the unregularized
smallest singular value exactly. Source: orthogonal diagonalization and the
Rayleigh minimum; atlas wishart-lambda-min-tail (operator limit bridge).

signature:
NLAlib.sigmaMin_transpose_sq_eq_zero_of_not_posDef.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {κ : Type u_2} [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ]
  [DecidableEq ι] (G : Matrix ι κ ℝ) (hnot : ¬(G * G.transpose).PosDef) : NLAlib.sigmaMin G.transpose ^ 2 = 0
name: NLAlib.sigmaMin_transpose_sq_eq_zero_of_not_posDef

signature:
NLAlib.sigmaMin_transpose_sq_le_frobSq.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {κ : Type u_2} [Fintype κ]
  [DecidableEq κ] [Nonempty ι] (G : Matrix ι κ ℝ) : NLAlib.sigmaMin G.transpose ^ 2 ≤ NLAlib.frobSq G
name: NLAlib.sigmaMin_transpose_sq_le_frobSq
doc:
The squared smallest singular value of the transposed rectangular matrix
is bounded by its squared Frobenius size. Source: spectral versus Frobenius
norm comparison; atlas wishart-lambda-min-tail (dominated limit helper).

signature: NLAlib.sineTruncation (c y : ℝ) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.sineTruncation
doc:
A smooth bounded value truncation. Source: the elementary sine/sinc
identities in Mathlib. Atlas: `gaussian-log-sobolev` (approximation helper).

signature: NLAlib.sineTruncation_eq_mul_sinc {c : ℝ} (hc : c ≠ 0) (y : ℝ) : NLAlib.sineTruncation c y = y * Real.sinc (c⁻¹ * y)
name: NLAlib.sineTruncation_eq_mul_sinc
doc:
The sine truncation is a sinc multiplier, including at zero. Source:
Mathlib's `Real.sinc_of_ne_zero`. Atlas: `gaussian-log-sobolev`.

signature: NLAlib.singularValueTailSq {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) (k : ℕ) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.singularValueTailSq
doc:
The squared singular-value tail after deleting the first `k` singular
values. Padding includes rectangular null directions and zero dimensions.
Horn–Johnson Theorem 7.4.9; atlas `eckart-young`.

signature:
NLAlib.singularValueTailSq_le_frobSq_sub_of_rank_le {m n : ℕ} (A B : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) (k : ℕ)
  (hB : B.rank ≤ k) : NLAlib.singularValueTailSq A k ≤ NLAlib.frobSq (A - B)
name: NLAlib.singularValueTailSq_le_frobSq_sub_of_rank_le
doc:
**Frobenius Eckart–Young lower bound.** Every rank-at-most-`k` real
competitor has squared error at least the singular-value tail.
Horn–Johnson Theorem 7.4.9; atlas `eckart-young`.

signature: NLAlib.singularValues {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) : ℕ → ℝ
name: NLAlib.singularValues
doc:
The singular values `σ₀ ≥ σ₁ ≥ ⋯ ≥ 0` of a real matrix, zero-indexed, padded with zeros:
`σ k = √(λ_k(AᵀA))` for `k < n` and `σ k = 0` for `k ≥ n`. Defined as Mathlib's
`LinearMap.singularValues` of `Matrix.toEuclideanLin A`. Atlas `svd`
(Horn–Johnson 2013, §2.6; HMT 2011, §2.1). Deviation: zero-indexed, indexed by `ℕ`.

signature: NLAlib.singularValues_antitone {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) : Antitone (NLAlib.singularValues A)
name: NLAlib.singularValues_antitone
doc: Singular values are listed in non-increasing order. Atlas `svd`.

signature:
NLAlib.singularValues_eq_linearMap {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.singularValues A k = (Matrix.toEuclideanLin A).singularValues k
name: NLAlib.singularValues_eq_linearMap
doc: Bridge to Mathlib's `LinearMap.singularValues`. Atlas `svd`.

name: NLAlib.singularValues_eq_of_eq_mul_rectDiag_mul
doc:
**Uniqueness of singular values** (Horn–Johnson 2013, Thm 2.6.3): if `A = U Σ_τ Vᵀ` with
`U`, `V` orthogonal and `τ` nonnegative and non-increasing, then `τ k = σ_k(A)` for every
`k < min m n`. Atlas `svd`.

signature:
NLAlib.singularValues_eq_zero_of_height_le {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) {k : ℕ} (hk : m ≤ k) :
  NLAlib.singularValues A k = 0
name: NLAlib.singularValues_eq_zero_of_height_le
doc: `σ k = 0` once `k ≥ m` (number of rows). Atlas `svd`.

signature:
NLAlib.singularValues_eq_zero_of_min_le {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) {k : ℕ} (hk : min m n ≤ k) :
  NLAlib.singularValues A k = 0
name: NLAlib.singularValues_eq_zero_of_min_le
doc: `σ k = 0` once `k ≥ min m n`. Atlas `svd`.

signature:
NLAlib.singularValues_eq_zero_of_rank_le {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) {k : ℕ} (hk : A.rank ≤ k) :
  NLAlib.singularValues A k = 0
name: NLAlib.singularValues_eq_zero_of_rank_le
doc: `σ k = 0` once `k ≥ rank A`. Atlas `svd`.

signature:
NLAlib.singularValues_eq_zero_of_width_le {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) {k : ℕ} (hk : n ≤ k) :
  NLAlib.singularValues A k = 0
name: NLAlib.singularValues_eq_zero_of_width_le
doc: `σ k = 0` once `k ≥ n` (number of columns). Atlas `svd`.

signature:
NLAlib.singularValues_le_specNorm {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.singularValues A k ≤ NLAlib.specNorm A
name: NLAlib.singularValues_le_specNorm
doc:
Every padded singular value is bounded by the spectral norm.
Horn–Johnson §5.6; atlas `norms-frob-spec`, `svd`.

signature:
NLAlib.singularValues_mul_orthogonal {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) {Q : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ}
  (hQ : Q.transpose * Q = 1) : NLAlib.singularValues (A * Q) = NLAlib.singularValues A
name: NLAlib.singularValues_mul_orthogonal
doc:
Singular values are invariant under right multiplication by an orthogonal matrix
(Horn–Johnson 2013, §2.6). Atlas `svd`.

signature:
NLAlib.singularValues_ne_zero_iff {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.singularValues A k ≠ 0 ↔ k < A.rank
name: NLAlib.singularValues_ne_zero_iff
doc:
The nonzero singular values are exactly the first `rank A` ones
(Horn–Johnson 2013, Thm 2.6.3 / §2.6.1). Atlas `svd`.

signature: NLAlib.singularValues_nonneg {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) (k : ℕ) : 0 ≤ NLAlib.singularValues A k
name: NLAlib.singularValues_nonneg
doc: Singular values are nonnegative. Atlas `svd`.

signature:
NLAlib.singularValues_orthogonal_mul {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) {Q : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) ℝ}
  (hQ : Q.transpose * Q = 1) : NLAlib.singularValues (Q * A) = NLAlib.singularValues A
name: NLAlib.singularValues_orthogonal_mul
doc:
Singular values are invariant under left multiplication by an orthogonal matrix
(Horn–Johnson 2013, §2.6). Atlas `svd`.

signature:
NLAlib.singularValues_pos_iff {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  0 < NLAlib.singularValues A k ↔ k < A.rank
name: NLAlib.singularValues_pos_iff
doc: The positive singular values are exactly the first `rank A` ones. Atlas `svd`.

signature:
NLAlib.singularValues_reindex_zero_eq_specNorm.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) :
  NLAlib.singularValues ((Matrix.reindex (Fintype.equivFin m) (Fintype.equivFin n)) A) 0 = NLAlib.specNorm A
name: NLAlib.singularValues_reindex_zero_eq_specNorm
doc:
The largest singular value of the explicit finite normalization is the
original spectral norm. Horn–Johnson §5.6; atlas `svd`, `norms-frob-spec`.
The reindex is temporary normalization for the parent `Fin`-only list API.

signature:
NLAlib.singularValues_transpose {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) :
  NLAlib.singularValues A.transpose = NLAlib.singularValues A
name: NLAlib.singularValues_transpose
doc: `σ(Aᵀ) = σ(A)` (Horn–Johnson 2013, §2.6). Atlas `svd`.

signature:
NLAlib.singularValues_zero_eq_specNorm {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) :
  NLAlib.singularValues A 0 = NLAlib.specNorm A
name: NLAlib.singularValues_zero_eq_specNorm
doc:
The largest sorted singular value equals the spectral norm. The padded
singular-value convention also covers matrices with zero rows or columns.
Atlas: `svd`, `norms-frob-spec`.

signature:
NLAlib.sketch_decomp.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4, u_5} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {q : Type u_3} {r : Type u_4}
  {s : Type u_5} [Fintype m] [Fintype q] [Fintype r] [DecidableEq q] [DecidableEq m] (Q : Matrix m q ℝ)
  (Qp : Matrix m r ℝ) (Ψ : Matrix m s ℝ) (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q)
  (hcomp : Q * Q.transpose + Qp * Qp.transpose = 1) :
  Ψ.transpose * A = Ψ.transpose * Q * (Q.transpose * A) + Ψ.transpose * Qp * (Qp.transpose * NLAlib.residual Q A)
name: NLAlib.sketch_decomp
doc:
First display in the proof of `lem:completion` (Chen–Persson):

NLAlib.variance_quadForm.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] {Ω : Type u_2} [MeasurableSpace Ω]

  {z : Ω → n → ℝ} (hmeas : ∀ (i : n), AEMeasurable (fun ω => z ω i) μ)
  (hindep : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun (fun i ω => z ω i) μ) (hmean : ∀ (i : n), ∫ (ω : Ω), z ω i ∂μ = 0)
  (hsq : ∀ (i : n), ∫ (ω : Ω), z ω i ^ 2 ∂μ = 1) (h4 : ∀ (i : n), MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun ω => z ω i ^ 4) μ)
  {m₄ : ℝ} (hm4 : ∀ (i : n), ∫ (ω : Ω), z ω i ^ 4 ∂μ = m₄) :
  ProbabilityTheory.variance (fun ω => NLAlib.quadForm A (z ω)) μ =
    ∑ i, ∑ j, A i j ^ 2 + ∑ i, ∑ j, A i j * A j i + (m₄ - 3) * ∑ i, A i i ^ 2
name: NLAlib.variance_quadForm
doc:
**Variance of Hutchinson's estimator** (general form). If the coordinates of `z` are
independent, centred, of unit variance and common fourth moment `m₄ = 𝔼[z_i⁴]`, then
`Var[zᵀ A z] = ∑ᵢⱼ A_ij² + ∑ᵢⱼ A_ij A_ji + (m₄ − 3) ∑ᵢ A_ii²` (mathematically the same as
`∑_{i≠j} (A_ij² + A_ij A_ji) + (m₄ − 1) ∑ᵢ A_ii²`; that form is not stated separately).
Source: Hutchinson (1989) [`hutch89`] (Rademacher case); Avron–Toledo (2011) [`at11`],
Lem 5 (Gaussian), Lem 6 (Rademacher). Atlas: `hutchinson-variance`.
Deviation: no symmetry of `A` assumed; general fourth moment `m₄` (`m₄ = 1` Rademacher,
`m₄ = 3` Gaussian).
